text.p: NatWest Markets, the investment banking arm of Britain's National Westminster Bank Plc, on Friday detailed a shake-up of its global debt markets division last year's takeover of U.S. bond house Greenwich Capital.

"The co-chief executives of the new global debt markets division are Gary Holloway and Chip Kruger," a NatWest spokeswoman told Reuters. She added that two senior managers, Johan Hattingh and Alby Cator had left as part of the changes.

Holloway and Kruger are both from Greenwich Capital. Holloway will be based in Greenwich in the U.S. and will be responsible for the U.S. and Asian operations while Kruger will be London-based and responsible for European debt markets operations.

The changes, which are not linked to recent revelations of 90 million pound ($143.5 million) losses in NatWest's options business, have also established other Greenwich managers in key positions. Greg Bowes, who built up Greenwich's London business before the NatWest takeover, has been made head of government bonds, repos and futures and options.

Other key appointments are Frank Canelas, who will head corporate bonds origination, sales, trading and research, Bruce Snider as head of asset-backed origination, structuring and trading and Phil Lotz, chief administrative officer for operations, IT and finance.

The NatWest spokeswoman said the shake-up played to both NatWest's and Greenwich's strengths. The changes, which were announced internally on Thursday, have created 10 main areas of responsibility within the debt markets division. ($ = 0.627 British Pounds)
